newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica's Vodacom subscriber base rises to 400,000.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica's Vodacom subscriber base rises to 400,000.

text.p: South African cellular network operator Vodacom said on Thursday it had signed up 400,000 subscribers in a total market of between 650,000 and 700,000 subscribers.

"South Africa's cellular market penetration has been remarkable and far exceeds African and South American countries. We also compare well to most European countries, but have not reached the level of penetration in countries such as Sweden and Finland," Vodacom managing director Alan Knott-Craig said.
Market sources said that the number of cellular connections per year in South Africa was double the number of fixed lines being installed.
But Knott-Craig said that the cellular industry was threatened by the instability and weakening of the rand.

Vodacom's network currently switches some seven million calls per day, accounting for 20 percent of the country's telephone traffic and eight percent of the African continent's. To date it had invested 2.8 billion rand in its network.
The company had about 1,500 base stations, covered almost 13,000 km of national roads and had a capacity for more than 500,000 subscribers.
Vodacom is 50 percent owned by telecommunications utility Telkom, with 31.5 percent held by the Vodafone Group plc of the UK and 18.5 percent by the Rembrandt Group Ltd.
